syllabus.summary: A sample interactive course used to verify the static renderer before connecting any external API.
outcomes: Interpret standard error and sampling distributions.
Apply core concepts to health data.

weeks.title: Sampling Distributions
weeks.overview: Connect samples, statistics and repeated sampling.

concepts.name: Population
concepts.definition: The full set of units about which an inference is made.

concepts.name: Sample
concepts.definition: A subset observed from the population.

concepts.name: Sampling Distribution
concepts.definition: The distribution of a statistic over repeated samples.

sections.title: Why repeated samples matter
sections.body: Different random samples produce different statistics. A sampling distribution describes that variation.

activities.title: Predict before calculating
activities.prompt: If sample size increases, what do you expect to happen to the variability of the sample mean?

quiz.question: What does a sampling distribution describe?
options: Variation of a statistic across repeated samples
Values of every individual in a population
quiz.rationale: A sampling distribution concerns the behavior of a statistic across repeated samples.

weeks.title: Standard Error
weeks.overview: Understand how sample size influences uncertainty.
objectives: Relate standard error to sample size.

concepts.name: Standard Error
concepts.definition: Describes the sampling variability of an estimator.

sections.title: SE versus SD
sections.body: SD describes variability in data values; SE describes uncertainty in an estimate such as a sample mean.

activities.title: Compare two studies
activities.prompt: Explain why a study with a larger sample can have a smaller standard error even if individual-level variability is similar.

quiz.question: Which quantity generally decreases as sample size increases?
quiz.rationale: For many estimators, standard error decreases as sample size grows.

review.title: Cumulative Review
review.instructions: Explain each concept without looking, then follow its prerequisite relationships.
prompts: Explain the chain Population → Sample → Sampling Distribution.
Contrast standard deviation with standard error.
